metaTitle: Sheng Ji celebrity stories: how to verify a claim
metaDescription: Celebrity stories about Sheng Ji need credible primary evidence. Learn to distinguish a public statement, original reporting, inference and rumor without using private people as testimonials.
metaKeywords: Sheng Ji celebrity rumor, Feng Shui claim verification, testimonials
h1: Sheng Ji celebrity stories: verify before treating a rumor as a case
heroSub: Check primary sources and consent · A famous name is not evidence of an outcome

items.h3: Interest in Feng Shui is not proof of this service
items.content: A public figure discussing Feng Shui does not establish that they received Sheng Ji, used this provider, or visited this site. Different traditions, practitioners and locations should not be conflated.

items.h3: An anonymous story proves neither identity nor outcome
items.content: Claims that an unnamed tycoon used a ritual require consent, reliable original reporting or independently checkable records. Even verified participation would not show that later wealth or health changes were caused by it.

sections.h2: How to check a specific claim

items.h3: Look for a direct public statement
items.content: Prefer the person’s own statement, an authorised representative or a credible original interview. Reposted articles, short-video captions and sales pages are weak sources.

Check the date and exact wording of the original source. A report that someone believes in Feng Shui is different from a report that they undertook a particular rite. Mark unsupported details as unverified.
Do not use a person’s name, photograph, health or family information as a testimonial without permission. Public figures retain privacy interests.

items.h3: Check the service, not the celebrity name
items.content: Confirm the provider, practitioner, location, total RMB price, deposit and balance, delivery records, rescheduling and refund terms in writing.

items.h3: Personal stories do not guarantee results
items.content: A cultural service cannot guarantee wealth, promotion, marriage, exam or health outcomes. Seek qualified professional advice where appropriate.
